name: RESILIENCE (ispace Mission 2)
left: Crash site (June 2025), with the TENACIOUS micro-rover it carried
fact: ispace's second lander rode to space on the same Falcon 9 as Firefly's Blue Ghost on 15 January 2025, flew past the Moon at about 8,400 km in February and entered lunar orbit on 6 May 2025. On 5 June 2025 its laser range finder was slow to give valid altitudes, so the lander could not slow down enough: the last telemetry came about 192 m above the surface, faster than expected. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imaged the impact site, a dark smudge with a faint bright halo.
capability: An external review board led by MIT and Keio University experts recommended terrain-relative navigation, better fault handling and more testing for ispace's later landers.
